newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's current account deficit $4.9 billion.
newsitem.headline: Israel's current account deficit $4.9 billion.

text.p: The current account deficit in Israel's balance of payments rose to $4.898 billion last year from $3.874 billion in 1995, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday.

The bureau said the increase in the current account deficit was due to a $3.1 billion increase in merchandise and service imports, which it said was only partly offset by a $1.4 billion in merchandise and service exports. Unilateral transfers also rose by $610 million.
The deficit was financed by net capital imports of $2.67 billion, down slightly from $2.72 billion in 1995. Capital exports grew to $1.9 billion from $1.6 billion in 1995.

Israel's net foreign debt at the end of 1996 edged down to $20.028 billion from $20.191 billion a year earlier. Liabilites grew to $48.06 billion from $45.19 billion but foreign assets rose to $28.03 billion from $24.19 billion.

The bureau said net foreign investment grew to $1.7 billion from $1.2 billion in 1995. Forerigners invested $2.36 billion, up from $1.91 billion in 1995, while Israelis invested $761 million abroad, compared with $670 million in 1995.
